questions.question: In total how many biosphere reserves are there in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**18**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• As of now, India has a total of **18 biosphere reserves** distributed across the country.
 
• These biosphere reserves are areas of terrestrial and coastal ecosystems promoting solutions to reconcile the conservation of biodiversity with its sustainable use.
 
• The **first biosphere reserve** in India was the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve, established in 1986.
 
• Some notable biosphere reserves include **Sundarbans, Nanda Devi, Nokrek, and Great Nicobar**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Biosphere Reserves**

 
 
• Biosphere reserves are areas of terrestrial and coastal/marine ecosystems or a combination thereof, which are internationally recognized within the framework of UNESCO's Man and the Biosphere (MAB) Programme.
 
• The main aim of biosphere reserves is to conserve biological and cultural diversity, and promote economic and social development through partnerships between people and nature.
 
• Biosphere reserves involve local communities and all interested stakeholders in planning and management.
 
• They integrate three main "functions": conservation of biodiversity, economic development, and logistic support for research and education.
 
 
 
• **Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve**
 
 
• It is the **first biosphere reserve** in India, established in 1986.
 
• The reserve encompasses parts of Tamil Nadu, Kerala, and Karnataka.
 
• The Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve is known for its rich biodiversity, including several endangered species of flora and fauna.
 
 
 
• **Sundarbans Biosphere Reserve**
 
 
• It is located in the Ganges Delta and is known for its unique mangrove forests.
 
• The Sundarbans is home to the famous Royal Bengal Tiger and many other species of wildlife.
 
• The area is also recognized for its role in protecting the coastal regions from cyclones and tidal surges.
 
 
 
• **Nanda Devi Biosphere Reserve**
 
 
• Situated in the state of Uttarakhand, it includes the Nanda Devi and Valley of Flowers National Parks.
 
• It is known for its diverse alpine flora and fauna, including several endangered species.
 
• The area is also a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

questions.question: Which country among the following declared 'climate emergency' in 2019?

• The declaration of a climate emergency typically involves commitments to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, transition to renewable energy, and implement sustainable practices across various sectors.

• Investments in renewable energy technologies are essential to achieving long-term sustainability and combating climate change.

• Sustainable practices involve using resources in a way that meets present needs without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs.
 
• This includes practices such as reducing waste, conserving water, and promoting energy efficiency.
 
• Adopting sustainable practices across all sectors is critical to ensuring environmental health and economic stability.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true with regard to the Election Commission of India?

options.text: It is Constituted every four years.
It is a Permanent constitutional body.
It is Constituted every six years.
It is Constituted every five years.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It is a Permanent constitutional body**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Election Commission of India is established by the Constitution of India under Article 324.
 
• It is a permanent body, which means it is not dissolved after a certain period and continues to function perpetually.
 
• The main responsibility of the Election Commission is to conduct free and fair elections in India at both the central and state levels.
 
• The Commission consists of the Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners, appointed by the President of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Constitutional Body:**

 
 
• A constitutional body is an organization established by the Constitution of a country.
 
• It derives its powers, functions, and responsibilities from the Constitution itself, making it an integral part of the country's governance framework.
 
 
 
• **Article 324:**
 
 
• Article 324 of the Indian Constitution provides for the establishment of the Election Commission of India.
 
• It vests the superintendence, direction, and control of elections in the Election Commission.
 
 
 
• **Chief Election Commissioner:**
 
 
• The Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) is the head of the Election Commission of India.
 
• The CEC is appointed by the President of India and holds office for a term of six years or until reaching the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier.
 
 
 
• **Functions of the Election Commission:**
 
 
• Conducting elections for the Parliament, State Legislatures, and the offices of the President and Vice-President in India.
 
• Preparing and updating the electoral rolls to ensure eligible voters are registered.
 
• Monitoring and regulating the conduct of political parties and candidates to ensure free and fair elections.
 
• Implementing the Model Code of Conduct during elections to maintain order and fairness.

questions.question: A boy walks along two adjacent sides of a rectangular field. If he walks along its diagonal, then he saves a distance equal to one-third of the larger side. Find the ratio of larger side to the smaller side.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A boy walks along two adjacent sides of a rectangular field.

If he walks along the diagonal, he saves a distance equal to one-third of the larger side.

**Let:**

Length of the larger side = L

Length of the smaller side = S

**Formula used:**

The distance saved by walking along the diagonal is:

Distance saved = (L + S) - √(L² + S²)

**According to the problem:**

(L + S) - √(L² + S²) = (1/3)L

**Calculation:**

⇒ (L + S) - (1/3)L = √(L² + S²)

⇒ (2/3)L + S = √(L² + S²)

Squaring both sides:

⇒ ((2/3)L + S)² = L² + S²

⇒ (4/9)L² + (4/3)LS + S² = L² + S²

⇒ (4/9)L² + (4/3)LS = L²

⇒ (4/9)L² - L² + (4/3)LS = 0

⇒ (-5/9)L² + (4/3)LS = 0

⇒ 5L² = 12LS

⇒ L/S = 12/5

**∴ The ratio of the larger side to the smaller side is 12:5.**

questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• COBOL is classified as a t**hird-generation programming language**, designed for **business** and **administrative** systems.
 
• COBOL stands for **"Common Business-Oriented Language"** and is primarily used for data processing in finance and government sectors.
 
• COBOL is known for its readability, using** English-like syntax**, which makes it easier for non-programmers to understand.
 
• COBOL is still widely used in legacy systems, especially in large-scale batch-processing systems for **banks** and** insurance **companies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **First-Generation Languages (1GL)**

 
 
• **Machine Language:** This generation involves machine-level programming, consisting of binary code (0s and 1s).
 
• Direct Hardware Interaction: Programmers write instructions that the CPU directly understands.
 
• **Example: **Binary code for early computers.
 
 
 
• **Second-Generation Languages (2GL)**
 
 
• **Assembly Language:** Uses mnemonics (symbolic code) for instructions, which are translated into machine code using an assembler.
 
• Low-Level Programming: Provides closer control over hardware, but is still difficult to work with.
 
• **Example: **Assembly Language.
 
 
 
• **Third-Generation Languages (3GL)**
 
 
• **High-Level Language: **Offers more abstraction from the hardware, allowing the programmer to focus on logic rather than machine code.
 
• Improved Readability and Portability: Code written in 3GL can run on different hardware systems with minimal changes.
 
• **Example:** COBOL, C, FORTRAN.
 
 
 
• **Fourth-Generation Languages (4GL)**
 
 
• **Application-Oriented: **These languages are designed to be more user-friendly, and often used for database queries and report generation.
 
• Minimal Programming Required: Aimed at reducing the complexity of software development by automating repetitive tasks.
 
• **Example: **SQL, MATLAB.
 
 
 
• **Fifth-Generation Languages (5GL)**
 
 
• **Logic-Based and AI-Oriented:** These languages are based on problem-solving using constraints rather than specific algorithms.
 
• AI and Expert Systems: They are used in artificial intelligence and machine learning.
 
• **Example: **Prolog, Mercury.

questions.question: If Y + 1over{}z = 1 and X + 1over{}y = 1, then what is the value of XYZ?

From **X + 1/Y = 1**, we get **X = (Y − 1)/Y**.

From **Y + 1/Z = 1**, we get **1/Z = 1 − Y**, which means **Z = 1/(1 − Y)**.

Multiply **X**, **Y**, and **Z**: **XYZ = [(Y − 1)/Y] × Y × [1/(1 − Y)]**.

**XYZ = (Y − 1) / (1 − Y) = −1**.

**∴ The correct answer is −1.**

⇒ **Z = 1 / (1 − Y)**

⇒ Now calculate **XYZ**: **XYZ = [(Y − 1) / Y] × Y × [1 / (1 − Y)]**

⇒ **XYZ = (Y − 1) / (1 − Y)**

⇒ **XYZ = −(1 − Y) / (1 − Y) = −1**

questions.question: If 3x + y = 5 and 4x - 3y = 2, then the ratio x : y is:

**Given:**

3x + y = 5

4x - 3y = 2

**Formula used:**

Simultaneous equations

**Calculation:**

Multiply the first equation by 3:

⇒ 3(3x + y) = 3(5)

⇒ 9x + 3y = 15

Now add this to the second equation:

⇒ 9x + 3y + 4x - 3y = 15 + 2

⇒ 13x = 17

⇒ x = 17/13

Substitute x = 17/13 into the first equation:

⇒ 3(17/13) + y = 5

⇒ 51/13 + y = 5

⇒ y = 5 - 51/13

⇒ y = (65 - 51)/13

⇒ y = 14/13

So, the ratio x : y is:

⇒ x : y = (17/13) : (14/13)

⇒ x : y = 17 : 14

**∴ The correct answer is option (2).**

questions.question: Find the third term in a sequence of positive numbers that will leave remainders 1, 2 and 5 when divide by 2, 3 and 6 respectively.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Find the third term in a sequence of positive numbers that will leave remainders 1, 2, and 5 when divided by 2, 3, and 6 respectively.

**Conditions:**

 
• x ≡ 1 (mod 2)
 
• x ≡ 2 (mod 3)
 
• x ≡ 5 (mod 6)

**Calculation:**

From the condition x ≡ 5 (mod 6), we know that:

 
• x can be expressed as x = 6k + 5 for some integer k.

Now substitute this into the second condition:

6k + 5 ≡ 2 (mod 3)

0k + 2 ≡ 2 (mod 3) (since 6 is divisible by 3)

This is always true.

Now substitute into the first condition:

6k + 5 ≡ 1 (mod 2)

0k + 1 ≡ 1 (mod 2) (since 6 is even)

This is also always true.

Now we can find the positive values of x:

Let k = 0, 1, 2, ...

For k = 0:

x = 6(0) + 5 = 5

For k = 1:

x = 6(1) + 5 = 11

For k = 2:

x = 6(2) + 5 = 17

Thus, the third term is:

x = 17

**The third term in the sequence is 17.**

questions.solution:
**Given:**

A rectangular room has an area 60 m² and perimeter 34 m.

**Formula used:**

Area (A) = l × w

Perimeter (P) = 2(l + w)

Diagonal (d) = sqrt{l² + w²}

**Calculation:**

l × w = 60

2(l + w) = 34

⇒ l + w = 17

We have two equations:

1) l × w = 60

2) l + w = 17

From equation 2:

w = 17 - l

Substitute into equation 1:

l(17 - l) = 60

⇒ 17l - l² = 60

⇒ l² - 17l + 60 = 0

Solve the quadratic equation:

l = dfrac{17 pm sqrt{17² - 4 times 60}}{2}

⇒ l = dfrac{17 pm sqrt{289 - 240}}{2}

⇒ l = dfrac{17 pm sqrt{49}}{2}

⇒ l = dfrac{17 pm 7}{2}

Possible values of l:

l = 12 or l = 5

If l = 12, then w = 17 - 12 = 5

If l = 5, then w = 17 - 5 = 12

In either case:

Diagonal (d) = sqrt{12² + 5²}

⇒ d = sqrt{144 + 25}

⇒ d = sqrt{169}

⇒ d = 13 m

**∴ The correct answer is option (3).**

questions.question: Corals are marine invertebrates within the class Anthozoa of the phylum__________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cnidaria**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Corals are marine invertebrates within the class **Anthozoa** of the phylum **Cnidaria**.
 
• Cnidarians are characterized by the presence of specialized cells known as **cnidocytes** that they use mainly for capturing prey.
 
• The phylum **Cnidaria** includes not only corals but also jellyfish, sea anemones, and hydra.
 
• Corals primarily form **symbiotic relationships** with algae called zooxanthellae, which provide them with energy through photosynthesis.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Phylum Cnidaria**

 
 
• Cnidaria is a phylum under the kingdom Animalia that includes around 10,000 species of aquatic animals.
 
• They are predominantly marine species but also include freshwater species.
 
• Cnidarians have a simple body plan with radial symmetry, a mouth, and tentacles.
 
• They exhibit two main forms: the polyp (e.g., sea anemones) and the medusa (e.g., jellyfish).
 
 
 
• **Anthozoa**
 
 
• Anthozoa is a class within the phylum Cnidaria that includes corals, sea anemones, and sea pens.
 
• They are exclusively marine animals.
 
• Unlike other cnidarians, anthozoans do not have a medusa stage in their life cycle.
 
• They are often colonial and can form extensive coral reefs which provide critical habitats for marine life.
 
 
 
• **Zooxanthellae**
 
 
• Zooxanthellae are a type of symbiotic algae that live within the tissues of corals.
 
• They perform photosynthesis and provide the coral with organic compounds, which serve as a major energy source for corals.
 
• This symbiotic relationship is essential for the growth and health of coral reefs.
 
• Coral bleaching occurs when corals expel their zooxanthellae due to stress conditions such as increased sea temperatures.
 
 
 
• **Cnidocytes**
 
 
• Cnidocytes are specialized cells unique to the phylum Cnidaria.
 
• They contain organelles called nematocysts, which can deliver a sting to capture prey or for defense.
 
• These cells play a crucial role in the feeding mechanism of cnidarians.
 
• The venom delivered by cnidocytes can vary from mild to extremely potent, depending on the species.
